document.title: Message to Mullah Omar (State 181837)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] Contains Mullah Omar's letter faxed to U.S. officials on 24 Sept 1998, which says bin Laden is 'just an excuse made by the U.S.', and the State Department reply. The reply uses 'with us or against us' language, saying those who harbor terrorists must accept responsibility for their actions.

persons.name: Mullah Mohammad Omar Mujahid
persons.role: Taliban leader, Amir-ul-Momeneen (Commander of the Faithful); author of 24 Sep 1998 faxed message to the US

mentions.quote: TRANSLATION OF MULLAH OMAR'S FAXED MESSAGE OF 9/24
WE UNDERSTAND THAT MULLAH OMAR DICTATED THE ENTIRE MESSAGE

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin

mentions.quote: IT IS ESSENTIAL USAMA BIN LADEN BE BROUGHT TO JUSTICE FOR HIS TERRORIST ACTS.

mentions.quote: ENSURE THIS RESPONSE GETS TO BOTH MULLAH OMAR AND MULLAH RABBANI ELEMENTS OF THE TALIBAN.

events.description: Six Plus Two foreign ministers adopt points including Taliban ceasing safehaven to terrorists; Clinton addresses UNGA.
Mullah Omar's faxed message (dated 23 Sep 1998, no. 110) to US leadership.
State Department instructs Embassy Islamabad to pass formal response to Mullah Omar and Rabbani elements, pressing on bin Ladin.
Six Plus Two foreign ministers adopt points of common understanding including that Taliban cease providing safehaven to international terrorists.
President Clinton addresses UN General Assembly urging action against terrorism.
Mullah Omar's faxed message (dated 23 Sep 1998) to the US leadership criticizing US policy and the bin Ladin issue.
State Department cable instructs Embassy Islamabad to deliver formal reply to Mullah Omar, demanding bin Ladin be brought to justice.
Mullah Omar dictates a message to the US government, relayed in State cable 181837. It says Taliban policy is Islamic and cannot be changed, calls the bin Ladin issue an excuse, and invites dialogue.

key_claims: The US sought confidential dialogue with the Taliban via the Islamabad embassy, prioritizing the bin Ladin issue.
The US said bin Ladin's group uses Afghan soil and threatens US citizens, and must be brought to justice.
The US would hold the Taliban responsible for further bin Ladin network terrorism while sanctuary continues.
Mullah Omar dictated a message calling the bin Ladin issue an excuse and defending Taliban policy as real Islam.
The State Department wanted the response to reach both Mullah Omar and Mullah Rabbani elements of the Taliban.
